remit: attack crowded ideas; prefer better ownership asymmetry
stance_summary: Verified: the crowded book is the energy-constrained global-hawk narrative, not a missing Canada hiking cycle. CORRA still prices +84bp by 2027-03 and +130.5bp by 2027-12 from a 2.29 overnight while Canada labor is 38, core is near 2%, CAD leveraged-fund shorts have already covered to the 99th one-year percentile of their net, and a Saudi STS workaround has reduced the oil-supply tail. Inference: that is a bad ownership entry into paying Canada. Unknown: CORRA futures open interest is null and CME positioning is unavailable, so this is not a claim that CRA specs are empty. Trade is short the implied-rate CORRA 2027 strip (receive Canada 2027) versus joining long AUDCAD, long JPY, or residual US 2Y/10Y spec shorts.

expression_comparison.rationale: The mispricing is the CORRA path, not a USD/CAD extreme. USDCAD is only 74.0th percentile 1y / 87.0th 5y, and CFTC CAD leveraged funds are still net short 39022 contracts, so a spot CAD-lower fade has to fight a remaining short-covering squeeze. Rates do not require CAD to sell versus USD; they require 2027 implied CORRA to reprice. Paying CORRA versus receiving AONIA to fade 5y-extreme AUDCAD is inferior because that RV is the crowded BoC-hike/housing-dove consensus and CA-AU 2Y is already -164.9bp at the 10.5th 5y percentile. Do not default to options: no premium/IV/strike mids.

context_build.causal_mechanism: Bank of Canada policy is being priced as an energy-pass-through hiking cycle even though the domestic labor and core-inflation channel does not look like a mid-cycle tightening economy. If that energy-hawk story is the consensus everyone already owns, 2027 implied CORRA is the object that has to cheapen when labor/core dominate and the oil tail shrinks.

context_build.known_vs_new_information: Known: Canada headline inflation at 3% with core near 2%; weak Canada labor (gauge 38) versus US labor 75; Fed hike was already >90% priced into the 2026-09-16 FOMC. New enough to re-open the ownership question now: BoC minutes flagging energy pass-through, the last-24h desk thesis that the energy shock constrains easing even where growth is softer, the 2026-09-17 SOFR step-up after the delivered Fed hike, CAD spec covering into that hawkish narrative, and the Saudi ship-to-ship workaround that reduces the extreme oil-supply tail. The energy-hawk story is no longer a secret; it is the position.
context_build.market_implied_assumption: CORRA 2027 prices a full tightening cycle from 2.29 toward about 3.40 on the 2027 H/M/U/Z average and about 3.65 by 2028, i.e. the BoC must hike through soft labor and near-2% core because energy pass-through and the global hawk keep the easing impulse shut.
context_build.market_assumption_disagreed_with: The priced assumption that is wrong is that Canada still needs ~80-136bp of additional hikes. Inference, not fact: once energy-pass-through is the owned narrative, residual oil-tail shrinkage and a 38 labor gauge make that path too much, not too little.
context_build.price_decomposition: Level versus change: Canada 2Y at 3.27 is 97.8th percentile on 1y but only 58.5th on 5y, so this is not a 5y cash-yield extreme. The marginal object is the 2027 implied-rate strip, where most of the +84 to +130.5bp of tightening versus overnight lives. Canada 2s10s is 56bp at the 0.60th 1y percentile, i.e. the front end has already sold off versus 10s. CA-US 2Y at -140bp is the 3.57th 1y percentile because the US 2Y (4.76, 100th 1y after a delivered hike) sold off more than Canada, not because CORRA 2027 is empty of hikes. Do not treat the 2Y percentile as a substitute for the CRA path.

historical_reference.regime_differences: The 2022-06-30 and 2023-04-14 +31bp analogs occurred while inflation was still clearly above a near-2% core and hiking cycles were live; those forward outcomes (+66bp and +83bp over 3m) are the crowded inference, not a base case. Current packet regime differences: CORRA overnight is still 2.29 (no delivered BoC hike comparable to the Fed's 25bp), Canada core is near 2%, labor gauge is 38 versus US 75, and the energy tail has a documented STS workaround. 5y Canada 2Y percentile 58.5 also differs from those mid-cycle highs. No analog in the packet maps 136bp of priced CORRA hikes onto a 38 labor gauge; that gap is stated rather than invented.

trade.structure: Equal-weight short implied-rate strip of MX three-month CORRA contracts 2027-03, 2027-06, 2027-09 and 2027-12 (CRAH27/CRAM27/CRAU27/CRAZ27). Paper family locked to CORRA; marks in implied-rate space (implied_rate = 100 minus futures price). Sidecar has zero open positions so this is a new OPEN, not an ADD.
trade.thesis: Fade the crowded energy-hawk / BoC-must-hike book by shorting 2027 implied CORRA (receiving Canada 2027). Verified: CRA prices +84bp by Mar-27 and +130.5bp by Dec-27 from 2.29 while Canada labor is 38 and core is near 2%; CAD specs have already covered to a 99th-percentile 1y net; the desk thesis says energy blocks easing even where growth is softer. Inference: that narrative is owned, so the better asymmetry is against further CA-rate upside, not with it. Unknown: CRA open interest and CME positioning, so this is not a claim the futures pit is empty. Explicitly not the trade: long AUDCAD at a 5y extreme, long JPY after a 99th-percentile leveraged-fund pile-in, or joining residual US duration shorts.
trade.mispricing: The market implies a Canada hiking cycle of roughly 80-136bp through 2027-28 that treats energy pass-through as binding. Packet facts (core near 2%, labor 38, CAD covering already extended, oil-tail workaround) say that cycle is the consensus overlay, not an unowned forecast.
why_now: CAD leveraged-fund covering of +16426 contracts to a 99.04th 1y net percentile as of 2026-09-15 shows the hawk/CAD-higher idea is already the flow.

BoC minutes on energy pass-through plus the last-24h desk thesis made that hawk the common G10 overlay, while SOFR's 2026-09-17 jump to 3.85 confirmed the Fed hike was delivered and is no longer the Canada-specific catalyst.
Saudi STS workaround the same week reduces the oil-supply tail used to justify pricing +130.5bp of CORRA hikes from 2.29.
Canada 2Y's -8bp on 2026-09-17 is the first sign the cash front end is no longer one-way, while 2027 CRA still holds the cycle.

catalysts: Canada inflation/labor prints that keep core near 2% and labor soft versus a 3.13-3.60 2027 CORRA path.
BoC communications that walk back energy-pass-through as a hiking trigger after the Saudi workaround.
Failure of remaining CAD shorts to squeeze 2027 implied CORRA even if USDCAD covering continues.
principal_risks: Packet analogs of a +31bp Canada 2Y month (2022-06-30 and 2023-04-14) saw +66bp and +83bp over the next 3m when hiking cycles were live; that is the main fundamental risk.
CORRA contract open_interest and volume are null and CME positioning is unavailable, so futures crowding is unknown.
A renewed oil shock that restores the energy-pass-through overlay.
Seat still pays official SOFR 3.85 ACT/360 on the full $100m allocation; a slow CORRA reprice can lose to funding.
CAD FX covering can continue even if this rates view is right, so do not size as if USDCAD must confirm immediately.
